groups.group0: Per-call output delta appended by original worker to retained prefix at slot+24; not a list of competing answers.
groups.group1: Current replaceable suffix at slot+104, concatenated after retained prefix in numeric consumption.
groups.counts: Group0 raw context signed halfword +94A8; group1 selected-chain depth minus group0 count minus one. Segment/output-position counts, not hypothesis ranks. In all observed numeric samples counts equal emitted code lengths.
groups.capacity: Each caller buffer has 16 uint16 slots; worker accessor loops consume at most 15 nonzero codes; consumer concatenation is bounded to 16 positions. Service fails closed on nonterminated 16-code output.
groups.ordering: Character/segment sequence order; no exposed rank ordering is established.

consumer.numeric_mapping: Subtract 0x30 per returned code, then value=10*value+digit; values outside 0..99 become 0xFFFF. No other code normalization is present on this mode-0 path.
consumer.secondary: 020A3FFC(ctx,group,index,buffer,16-index,null,null) selects a second representation of the same segment; original consumer uses its first code per position. No second-best or probability claim.
consumer.expected_policy: Calculations sets +31C=2 and +224=expected at 02026C6C..02026C7C through 02052260. With one position and expected<10, secondary may replace primary only when equal to expected and not 1. With two positions and expected>=10, per-position substitution uses expected tens/units; original guard on units is secondary tens !=1. No arbitrary candidate-set membership search.
consumer.metadata: Worker also reads per-position metric via 020A3FB8 and contributing stroke IDs/count via 020A3F2C. Mode-0 selection does not rank by metric. Contribution count can affect a three-stroke/two-digit 4-or-5 delay rule.
consumer.publication: After numeric selection, +364 countdown controls publication. For single-digit matching 7 or 9 it is 1 and decrements to zero in the same update; caller then reads +320 for submission. Matching 4/5 may delay 11 updates after one stroke; ordinary mismatch uses 41. Task X does not execute submission.
consumer.scalar_equivalence: Legacy scalar first group-1 code is not generally equivalent to complete original consumption; preserved for compatibility.

preprocessing.original: Once-per-update held sampling including identical positions; clamp to selected rectangle; transform (x,y)->(y,255-x); nonempty release creates count/pointer descriptor in recorded order, without sentinel/contact/timing payload. Limits 4096 points and 32 descriptors.
preprocessing.host_differences: Deduplicates consecutive identical positions; rejects points outside host canvas instead of original rectangle clamping. All frozen points are interior to both rectangles. Task S A/B proves duplicate equivalence only for known 4, not all handwriting.
preprocessing.missing_step: No additional title-side preprocessing proven between accumulation and 020A41A0. Internal conversion/normalization remains executed by the original recognizer; 020A4718 calls 020B387C with internal point limit 32.
preprocessing.changes: None; preserve exact known-4 adapter/configuration. No universal claim that sampling density never matters.

miss_classification.7: Combination: strong stroke-boundary/segmentation sensitivity on the same geometry; production scalar truncates final 51 to 5 and omits expected-dependent first-release 1/7 substitution. Crossbar-first ordering does not fix final 51. Not merely a ranked candidate-selection error.
miss_classification.9: Combination: strong stroke-boundary sensitivity (joined identical loop/tail yields 9); direction sensitivity (reversed loop yields final 0); expected-dependent first-release 0/9 substitution omitted by scalar. Tail-first still ends as 4. Final W-anchor 4/0 does not contain 9.
miss_classification.limits: No post-observation sample edits; this small corpus does not establish arbitrary handwriting accuracy or eliminate all density-related effects.

readiness: Yes for a separately authorized, narrowly bounded answer-entry integration experiment using this proven character/expected-policy contract and preserved isolation. Not general handwriting validation; original early-publication behavior must be an explicit design decision.
recommended_next_task: Task Y (separate authorization): bounded answer-entry integration for one controlled Calculations problem, with explicit character-sequence/secondary-code policy and release/publication timing, frozen gestures, exact-title Policy A service, and no completion scoring, save/history, menu integration or optimization.
